module_title: Tribes of India - Constitutional Basis and 2011 Census Stats
introduction: India is home to a vast array of indigenous communities known as 'Adivasis' or 'Scheduled Tribes' (STs). These groups are historically characterized by geographical isolation, distinctive culture, and backwardness. At this level, we focus on the core numbers and the legal framework that defines tribal identity in India.

core_concepts.title: Constitutional Definitions
core_concepts.description: Article 366 (25) defines Scheduled Tribes. However, 'Article 342' is more critical as it empowers the President of India to specify the tribes or tribal communities in any State or Union Territory to be deemed as Scheduled Tribes.

core_concepts.title: Demographic Snapshot
core_concepts.description: According to the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes constitute '8.6%' of India's total population. By 'Absolute Number', Madhya Pradesh has the highest tribal population, followed by Maharashtra and Odisha.

core_concepts.title: India's Top 3 Largest Tribes
core_concepts.description: 1. Bhil: The largest tribal group in India (approx. 38% of total ST population). 2. Gond: The second largest group. 3. Santhal: The third largest group, primarily concentrated in Eastern India.

core_concepts.title: States/UTs with NO ST Population
core_concepts.description: According to the 2011 Census, five regions in India have 'Zero' Scheduled Tribe population: Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, and Puducherry.

important_entities.name: The Bhil Tribe
important_entities.significance: Bhils are famously known as the 'Bow Men of India'. They are widely distributed across Western India, including Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra, often living around the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If asked which state has the 'Most' STs, it is Madhya Pradesh. If asked which state/UT has the 'Highest Percentage' of STs, the answer is 'Lakshadweep' (94.8%) among UTs and 'Mizoram' (94.4%) among States.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Bhil > Gond > Santhal. Use the initials to remember the hierarchy of population.

exam_strategy_tips: Remember that STs make up 8.6% of the population, while SCs (Scheduled Castes) make up 16.6%. Do not swap these numbers.
The fact that Punjab and Haryana have no STs is a high-yield 'Elimination' point for MCQs.
